\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{روزہ} (rozā)}{روزہ (rozā)}]{\ur{روزہ} (rozā) — a fast (from dawn to dusk)}

\label{lesson:UR-C322-roza}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for gathered together, then the Urdu for a spectacle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{روزہ}}
\textbf{\ur{روزہ}} — \emph{rozā} — \textquotedblleft{}a fast (from dawn to dusk)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{آج} \ur{روزہ} \ur{رکھا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{us ne āj rozā rakhā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He fasted today.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{روزہ}} (\emph{rozā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{rōza}, \textquotedblleft{}a fast\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{rōz}, \textquotedblleft{}a day\textquotedblright{}, the word inside \textbf{\ur{روز}}. A fast is kept: \textbf{\ur{روزہ} \ur{رکھا}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rozā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rozā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{us ne āj rozā rakhā.} — He fasted today.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for gathered together, then the Urdu for a spectacle, then say \emph{rozā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{روزہ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A fast (from dawn to dusk)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سحری} (sahrī)}{سحری (sahrī)}]{\ur{سحری} (sahrī) — the meal before dawn (in a fast)}

\label{lesson:UR-C322-sahri}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a spectacle, then the Urdu for a fast.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سحری}}
\textbf{\ur{سحری}} — \emph{sahrī} — \textquotedblleft{}the meal before dawn (in a fast)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ہم} \ur{نے} \ur{سویرے} \ur{سحری} \ur{کھائی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ham ne savere sahrī khāī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We ate the pre-dawn meal early in the morning.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سحری}} (\emph{sahrī}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{saḥar}, \textquotedblleft{}the time before dawn\textquotedblright{}, with the ending \emph{-ī}: the meal eaten then, before the fast begins.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{افطاری} (iftārī)}{افطاری (iftārī)}]{\ur{افطاری} (iftārī) — the food that breaks a fast}

\label{lesson:UR-C322-iftari}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a fast, then the Urdu for the meal before dawn.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{افطاری}}
\textbf{\ur{افطاری}} — \emph{iftārī} — \textquotedblleft{}the food that breaks a fast\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{سب} \ur{نے} \ur{مل} \ur{کر} \ur{افطاری} \ur{کی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sab ne mil kar iftārī kī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Everyone broke the fast together.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{افطاری}} (\emph{iftārī}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ifṭār}, \textquotedblleft{}a breaking of the fast\textquotedblright{}, with the ending \emph{-ī}: the dates, fruit and fried food set out at sunset.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{دعا} (duā)}{دعا (duā)}]{\ur{دعا} (duā) — a prayer of asking; a blessing}

\label{lesson:UR-C322-dua}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for the meal before dawn, then the Urdu for the food that breaks a fast.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{دعا}}
\textbf{\ur{دعا}} — \emph{duā} — \textquotedblleft{}a prayer of asking; a blessing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دادی} \ur{نے} \ur{سب} \ur{کے} \ur{لیے} \ur{دعا} \ur{کی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dādī ne sab ke liye duā kī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Grandmother prayed for everyone.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{duʿā}, \textquotedblleft{}a calling upon\textquotedblright{}: asking God for something. \textbf{\ur{نماز}} is the set prayer; \textbf{\ur{دعا}} is your own.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{خیرات} (khairāt)}{خیرات (khairāt)}]{\ur{خیرات} (khairāt) — charity; alms}

\label{lesson:UR-C322-khairat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for the food that breaks a fast, then the Urdu for a prayer of asking.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{خیرات}}
\textbf{\ur{خیرات}} — \emph{khairāt} — \textquotedblleft{}charity; alms\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{ابو} \ur{ہر} \ur{سال} \ur{خیرات} \ur{دیتے} \ur{ہیں۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{abbū har sāl khairāt dete haiṅ.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Dad gives to charity every year.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{خیرات}} (\emph{khairāt}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{khayrāt}, \textquotedblleft{}good deeds, good things\textquotedblright{}, a plural; in Urdu it is what is given to the poor.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}
